The per-end variants (`rounding1`, `chamfer_angle`, …) that sit beside `EdgeTreatment` on ten constructors are B-3's duplication and were addressed by T31 from the other end: **67 façade defaults were `None` where a backend had a real value**, so the backend's default decided anything the caller left out and the two could resolve the same call differently. They are the façade's now, and `test_the_facade_owns_every_shared_default` keeps them there. Twenty-four remain `None` for a reason, in two groups: `res` (an ambient control — nothing to inherit means the backend's facet default is the answer, R-7) and `anchor` on the cylinders (the right value depends on `center`, so the backend computes it). The façade's parameter duplication (B-3) is untouched — a group removes three parameters from a signature that has forty. |
| 7a | **PLAN D-P4 / DOC-2** | **Closed by T35 and T39.** D-P4 has asked for a complete `Args:` on every public callable since it was written and nothing had ever checked: **313 public callables taking 1307 parameters documented none of them.** All of them do now, and the check is a plain assertion rather than a budget. **The method is the part worth keeping**, because the obvious one is unsound: harvesting "the most common wording for this parameter name" put a polyhedron's insphere radius on `cylindrical_extrude` and a cube-truss size on its `size`, and that attempt was reverted whole. What is safe is a *specific* source — the same-named function's own wording (the SDF backend mirrors the CSG API, PAR-1), the function a wrapper delegates to, and a hand-written vocabulary **per module**, because a name is reliably one thing inside one module and not across the library. 439 descriptions were written that way for the remaining 256, and reviewing the output still caught `quaternion_slerp(q1, q2, t)` documented as "the second and third quaternion". |
| 7b | **PLAN O-6b** | **Closed by T36.** `flat.text()` declared `anchor: str = "baseline"` while the other eight 2-D constructors take the anchor language, and it was the one `placement=` could not be wired into. It was never an anchor: the body read `valign if valign is not None else anchor`, so it was a **second spelling of `valign`** with a different default — a parallel vocabulary that also duplicated a parameter sitting beside it. `valign` owns the baseline default now and `anchor` is `Anchor | Sequence[float] | None`, applied to the finished text's box after the typographic alignment has placed it. `None` keeps that typographic placement, which is the usual answer for text and what every existing call gets. All nine 2-D constructors now take `placement=`.

The named styles are cut into the cap's outer wall now, inset so the knurl takes material out of the nominal diameter rather than growing outside it. The guard scans the package for anything declaring `texture=` and builds it with and without one, so a new declarer that ignores it fails rather than joining the list quietly. |
| 8 | **C-23** (new) / **C-20** | **Closed by T33.** C-20 made the contract cover the whole object and said nothing about the cover meaning anything: **48 of the 90 members were declared `(*args: Any, **kwargs: Any)`** — found by name, checked not at all, so a caller following this project's own typing advice got every argument accepted including the wrong ones. Both families were loose for the same reason in the end — nobody had written the signatures out. The distribution family was obvious once looked at: all four implementations inherit one `Distributable` mixin and agree exactly. The attachment family *looked* like a harder case, because the SDF backend refuses it with a `(*_args: Any, **_kwargs: Any)` stub (PAR-3) and a loose implementation seems to force a loose contract. It does not: that form satisfies any protocol signature, so the contract was always free to declare the real one. 63 of 90 typed, and `base.attach("top", boss)` — C-20's own worked example, with the anchor mistyped — is a checker error instead of a silent pass. The remaining 27 are PLAN T-6c's genuine case, on a list that only shrinks.

It is a *renderer* hint about ray crossings; a distance field has no use for it and now ignores it, as B-9's tessellation carve-out says it may (C-17, C-21). **The layering edges stay**, and their reason is now measured rather than assumed: `Extrudable` is CSG machinery living correctly at L3 and *inherited* by two L2 geometry types. Closing it means `Path2D`/`Path3D` not carrying these methods at all, which is an API decision rather than a move.

**T52 then tried to move `Extrudable` down to L2 beside its two siblings, and could not.** `Sweepable` and `Roundable` are at L2 because they build a neutral `VNF` and call `.polyhedron()` on it, which needs no backend import — `skin` has one upward edge in the whole module and `rounding` has none. `Extrudable` composes *native* primitives (`pythonscad.cube`, `pythonscad.square`) with booleans, so it needs `Bosl2Solid` to hand the result back, **and the backend protocol has no way to adopt an already-composed native object** — it offers `constructor`, `construct`, `polyhedron`, the booleans, the extrudes and `stroke`, all of them building operations. The move traded two runtime edges for four deferred ones and was reverted. What is kept is the reason: the debt list said *"the mixin lives in an L3 module"*, which reads like an accident of filing, and now says the measured fact — **it composes native geometry, so it is backend machinery, and an L2 path type inherits backend machinery.** T52 then said closing it meant rewriting the two methods to produce a VNF, "a geometry rewrite rather than a move". **T54 measured that rewrite and it is worse: a feature removal.** A VNF sweep needs the cross-section as *points*, and these two exist precisely to take a profile that is not one — `path_extrude`'s own docstring says so, and a disjoint two-part profile builds here while `path_sweep` refuses it outright. Nor can the point-list subset be delegated and the rest kept native: `path_extrude` mitres its segments and `path_sweep` uses a rotation-minimising frame, so the two build *different geometry* for the same profile and the one call would mean two things. **This edge is the price of a capability, not deferred tidying**, and a test pins the capability so nobody discovers that by removing it.

**T53 took `regions -> shapes3d`, and it does not close either — for a third distinct reason.** `Region.debug_region(vertices=True)` numbers each vertex with `text3d`, which renders a font and is CSG-only. It cannot go through the façade because **`pybosl2.solid` is by design "the primitives *both* backends expose"** — 22 CSG-only names are exported top-level outside it, and adding one would make the façade mean something else. What was wrong is what the call *said*: it surfaced `'pybosl2.shapes3d.extrusions.text3d' is not supported`, an internal path three frames down, where the outline itself builds happily on either backend. The labels refuse under their own name now, on the option, the way `cyl(teardrop=)` does — and the import moved into the branch, so `import pybosl2.regions` no longer drags a backend module in for a debug helper most callers never touch. **The same feature turned out to be written twice**, in `Region.debug_region` and `Path2D.debug_polygon`, and a one-path region *delegates* to the second: fixing the first alone left the commonest case still reporting the old message, which the tests caught. One shared rule now, in `_helpers`. **T55 moved the three that are not going away out of the debt list.** `spec/layers.toml` has a `[capability_edges]` section now: upward edges that buy something the layer below cannot have, which is a different thing from work nobody has done yet, and a debt figure that mixes the two stops meaning anything. **What keeps it from becoming a dumping ground is `pinned_by`:** every entry names a test that holds the capability in place, so the claim "this edge buys something" is checked rather than asserted, and the next person who thinks the edge is removable finds out what it costs first. The check requires the test to exist *and* to mention the edge's source, and an edge may not be listed as both debt and architecture. **8 known violations remain**, down from 16 when this was first measured — 4 were never debt (typing-only), 1 was fixed (`arc` moved to the layer it belonged in), and 3 are architecture with the receipts to say so.

**8 remain**, of which one is runtime: `path2d`/`path3d -> miscellaneous` (the `Extrudable` mixin sits in L3 and is inherited by L2 types) and `regions -> shapes3d` (`Region.text3d`). |

## 13. Change process
1. A change altering a public signature MUST cite the requirement it serves in the commit body
   (`feat(solid): ambient resolution defaults — R-4`).
2. Adding a required parameter to an existing public callable is a breaking change and needs a
   default or a deprecation path.
3. Adding a façade shape follows B-7 and the parity rules in §7.1.
4. This document is updated in the same commit as any change to §4 (layering), §6 (subsystems),
   §7 (backends), or §8 (defaults). Language-level rules change in [PLAN.md](PLAN.md) instead.
5. **Requirement IDs are permanent.** Numbers are never reused or renumbered: a new requirement
   appends to its series, and a withdrawn one is struck through with the reason. Section numbers
   may move; IDs are what commits, tests and reviews cite.
